macroProcesses.name: Strategy & Governance Alignment
macroProcesses.objective: Translate corporate strategy into an approved annual L&D plan and budget envelope.
macroProcesses.trigger: Annual strategy cycle opened, or board publishes revised corporate objectives.
macroProcesses.terminal: Annual L&D plan approved by the Steering Committee and locked, linked to strategic objectives.

macroProcesses.name: Skills & Competency Management
macroProcesses.objective: Maintain the competency framework and a validated skills inventory for every employee.
macroProcesses.trigger: New or revised competency framework, or a scheduled skills assessment campaign.
macroProcesses.terminal: Validated skills inventory with a proficiency level per employee and competency.

macroProcesses.name: Needs Analysis & Diagnosis
macroProcesses.objective: Turn skills gaps, demands and diagnostic findings into a validated training needs register.
macroProcesses.trigger: Validated skills inventory or consolidated demand repository becomes available.
macroProcesses.terminal: Training needs register validated by the Head of L&D and released to report elaboration.

macroProcesses.name: Training Engineering Report & Roadmap Elaboration
macroProcesses.objective: Produce the flagship Training Engineering Report and the prioritized training roadmap.
macroProcesses.trigger: Validated needs register plus feeder outputs (diagnostic, demand, GPEC, SWOT, prioritized plan) are available.
macroProcesses.terminal: Training Engineering Report and roadmap approved and published to design and delivery.

macroProcesses.name: Learning Design & Curriculum Engineering
macroProcesses.objective: Convert roadmap themes into curriculum maps, learning paths and approved design documents.
macroProcesses.trigger: An approved roadmap theme is assigned to an instructional designer.
macroProcesses.terminal: Design document and learning path approved and released to content development.

macroProcesses.name: Content & Resource Management
macroProcesses.objective: Develop, review, publish and maintain learning content assets.
macroProcesses.trigger: An approved design document requires content assets.
macroProcesses.terminal: Content assets published to the catalog with visibility and competency tags set.

macroProcesses.name: Learning Delivery & Implementation
macroProcesses.objective: Schedule and deliver training across all modalities.
macroProcesses.trigger: A published learning path or module is scheduled for delivery.
macroProcesses.terminal: Session closed with attendance and completion recorded.

macroProcesses.name: Learner Experience & Engagement
macroProcesses.objective: Deliver a personalized, engaging learner journey.
macroProcesses.trigger: A learner has validated gaps or an assigned learning path.
macroProcesses.terminal: Learner journey active with recommendations accepted or dismissed and feedback captured.

macroProcesses.name: Assessment & Evaluation
macroProcesses.objective: Measure training effectiveness and skill progression (Kirkpatrick Levels 1-3).
macroProcesses.trigger: A session or learning path is completed.
macroProcesses.terminal: Evaluation results recorded and skill progression computed per learner.

macroProcesses.name: Reporting & Analytics
macroProcesses.objective: Provide KPIs, dashboards and exportable reports to every audience.
macroProcesses.trigger: Scheduled refresh or on-demand report request.
macroProcesses.terminal: Report or dashboard delivered to its audience within RBAC scope.

macroProcesses.name: Administration & Operations
macroProcesses.objective: Run training logistics and maintain accurate training records.
macroProcesses.trigger: Session logistics request or training record correction request.
macroProcesses.terminal: Logistics confirmed and training records reconciled for the period.

macroProcesses.name: Learning Culture & Knowledge Management
macroProcesses.objective: Grow a learning culture through a knowledge base, communities and lessons learned.
macroProcesses.trigger: Knowledge worth sharing is identified, or a record reaches closure.
macroProcesses.terminal: Knowledge article or REX entry published and indexed for retrieval.

macroProcesses.name: Talent & Career Development
macroProcesses.objective: Enable career progression through defined career paths and individual development plans.
macroProcesses.trigger: Annual career review, or an employee requests a development plan.
macroProcesses.terminal: Individual development plan agreed and succession readiness updated.

macroProcesses.name: Compliance & Certification Management
macroProcesses.objective: Keep the workforce compliant with valid mandatory training and certifications.
macroProcesses.trigger: A regulatory requirement is registered or a certification approaches expiry.
macroProcesses.terminal: Every in-scope employee holds a valid certification, with audit evidence retained.

macroProcesses.name: Vendor & Partner Ecosystem Management
macroProcesses.objective: Manage training vendors from selection to payment.
macroProcesses.trigger: A training need requires an external provider.
macroProcesses.terminal: Vendor paid against a matched purchase order, invoice and attendance.

macroProcesses.name: Data, AI & Integration Governance
macroProcesses.objective: Govern integrations, data quality, retention and AI use across the platform.
macroProcesses.trigger: Administrator registers an integration, a synchronisation runs, or the AI governance review is due.
macroProcesses.terminal: Integrations healthy, data governed under retention rules and AI use cases activated per scope.

macroProcesses.name: Identity, Access & Security Management
macroProcesses.objective: Control who can access what, and protect sessions and credentials.
macroProcesses.trigger: Administrator action or HRIS/SSO provisioning event (joiner, mover, leaver).
macroProcesses.terminal: User access matches role assignments, and access violations are logged and reviewed.

macroProcesses.name: Financial & Budget Management
macroProcesses.objective: Plan, track and close the L&D budget, including OFPPT refunds.
macroProcesses.trigger: Budget envelope approved for the plan year.
macroProcesses.terminal: Fiscal period closed with actuals reconciled and refund claims submitted.

macroProcesses.name: Change Management & Adoption
macroProcesses.objective: Drive sustained adoption of the platform and of new learning practices.
macroProcesses.trigger: A plan, platform release or new practice requires user adoption.
macroProcesses.terminal: Adoption targets met, or reinforcement actions recorded for lagging groups.

macroProcesses.name: Quality, Risk & Continuous Improvement
macroProcesses.objective: Improve processes and mitigate risk through governed actions.
macroProcesses.trigger: A risk, non-conformity or improvement opportunity is identified.
macroProcesses.terminal: Action completed and its effectiveness evaluated by a different user.

macroProcesses.name: Learning Support & Coaching
macroProcesses.objective: Provide coaching and learning support to individuals.
macroProcesses.trigger: A learner or manager requests coaching.
macroProcesses.terminal: Coaching engagement closed with outcomes evaluated.

macroProcesses.name: Extended Enterprise & External Training
macroProcesses.objective: Train and certify partners, resellers and customers.
macroProcesses.trigger: A partner or customer programme is launched.
macroProcesses.terminal: External learners certified and revenue recorded.

macroProcesses.name: Localization, Accessibility & Inclusion
macroProcesses.objective: Make learning available in English, French and Arabic, accessible and inclusive.
macroProcesses.trigger: A module is designed or content is published for a multilingual or diverse audience.
macroProcesses.terminal: Localized, accessible content published and participation equity reviewed.

macroProcesses.name: AI-Powered Personalization & Adaptive Learning
macroProcesses.objective: Adapt learning content, pace and pathway to each learner.
macroProcesses.trigger: Personalization is activated for a scope and a learner starts a path.
macroProcesses.terminal: Adapted path in use, with acceptance tracked and settings tuned.

macroProcesses.name: Microlearning & Learning in the Flow of Work
macroProcesses.objective: Deliver short learning capsules where work happens.
macroProcesses.trigger: A capsule is needed for a task, procedure or reminder.
macroProcesses.terminal: Capsule consumed, measured, and retained or retired.

macroProcesses.name: Social & Collaborative Learning Networks
macroProcesses.objective: Enable peer learning through cohorts and moderated discussion.
macroProcesses.trigger: A cohort or community of practice is launched.
macroProcesses.terminal: Active group with moderated exchanges and endorsed answers.

macroProcesses.name: Gamification & Engagement Mechanics
macroProcesses.objective: Increase engagement and completion through points, badges and challenges.
macroProcesses.trigger: Gamification is activated for a population or programme.
macroProcesses.terminal: Rules active, awards granted and uplift reviewed.

macroProcesses.name: Predictive Learning Analytics & Intelligence
macroProcesses.objective: Anticipate skill gaps and learner risk before they materialize.
macroProcesses.trigger: Scheduled prediction run or analyst request.
macroProcesses.terminal: Predictions reviewed and preventive actions created where warranted.

macroProcesses.name: Content Curation & Aggregation Engine
macroProcesses.objective: Discover, curate and maintain internal and external content.
macroProcesses.trigger: Provider catalogs refresh or a curation request is raised.
macroProcesses.terminal: Curated collections published and outdated items retired.

macroProcesses.name: Immersive Learning (VR/AR/Simulation)
macroProcesses.objective: Provide safe-to-fail practice through simulation.
macroProcesses.trigger: A high-risk or high-cost task requires practice.
macroProcesses.terminal: Simulation performance recorded as competency evidence.

macroProcesses.name: Skills-Based Talent Marketplace & Internal Mobility
macroProcesses.objective: Match internal talent to internal opportunities.
macroProcesses.trigger: An internal opening is published.
macroProcesses.terminal: Candidate selected, with a reskilling plan where gaps remain.

macroProcesses.name: Learning ROI & Business Impact Measurement
macroProcesses.objective: Validate ROI and business impact of training themes.
macroProcesses.trigger: A theme reaches its evaluation date or finance requests an ROI study.
macroProcesses.terminal: ROI study reviewed with finance and impact report published.

macroProcesses.name: User-Generated Content & Peer Knowledge Sharing
macroProcesses.objective: Let employees share know-how as reviewed content.
macroProcesses.trigger: An employee submits content.
macroProcesses.terminal: Approved content published with author credit and sent to curation.

macroProcesses.name: Expert Knowledge Capture & Transfer
macroProcesses.objective: Capture institutional knowledge before experts leave.
macroProcesses.trigger: An expert's departure or retirement is within the capture horizon.
macroProcesses.terminal: Knowledge captured and transfer to the successor validated.

macroProcesses.name: Onboarding & Rapid Upskilling
macroProcesses.objective: Accelerate new hires to productivity.
macroProcesses.trigger: A new hire's start date is confirmed.
macroProcesses.terminal: Onboarding closed with time-to-productivity recorded.

macroProcesses.name: Consulting Engagement Management
macroProcesses.objective: Manage a training-engineering consulting engagement from kickoff to closure.
macroProcesses.trigger: Signed purchase order for a consulting engagement.
macroProcesses.terminal: Engagement closed with client acceptance and REX recorded.

macroProcesses.name: Multi-Axis Organizational Diagnostic
macroProcesses.objective: Diagnose the organization on five axes to ground the training plan.
macroProcesses.trigger: Engagement kickoff completed, or internal diagnostic requested.
macroProcesses.terminal: Validated diagnostic findings per axis.

macroProcesses.name: Organizational Maturity Assessment (CMM-Based)
macroProcesses.objective: Assess L&D process maturity on a five-level CMM scale.
macroProcesses.trigger: Diagnostic phase of an engagement or annual maturity review.
macroProcesses.terminal: Maturity profile reported and target maturity agreed.

macroProcesses.name: Training Plan Impact Study (N-1)
macroProcesses.objective: Evaluate the impact of the previous year's plan.
macroProcesses.trigger: Start of a new planning cycle with an N-1 plan on record.
macroProcesses.terminal: Impact conclusions fed into the strategy update.

macroProcesses.name: Multi-Site / Multi-Entity Training Plan Deployment
macroProcesses.objective: Adapt and deploy the approved plan across sites and entities.
macroProcesses.trigger: Approved group-level plan to be deployed on several sites.
macroProcesses.terminal: Site plans deployed with consolidated status monitored.

macroProcesses.name: External Training Plan Validation & Regulatory Compliance
macroProcesses.objective: Submit and validate training plans with regulatory bodies (e.g. OFPPT, GIAC-Agro).
macroProcesses.trigger: Approved plan requires regulatory submission for validation or refund.
macroProcesses.terminal: Regulator decision recorded and evidence archived.

macroProcesses.name: Leadership Maturity Assessment & Development
macroProcesses.objective: Assess and develop leaders across five maturity levels.
macroProcesses.trigger: Leadership review cycle or promotion to a leadership role.
macroProcesses.terminal: Leadership development plan in place and maturity reassessed.

macroProcesses.name: Strategic & Competitive Intelligence
macroProcesses.objective: Analyze the external business environment to inform training strategy.
macroProcesses.trigger: Annual strategy cycle or executive request for market positioning analysis.
macroProcesses.terminal: Validated competitive intelligence report feeding L&D strategy and organizational diagnostic.

sipoc.goals: Analyze the external business environment (competitive forces, market trends, regulatory changes, technological shifts) to inform training strategy and ensure L&D aligns with market realities.
sipoc.suppliers: Executive leadership, strategy team, market research firms, industry associations, regulatory bodies, competitive intelligence tools
sipoc.inputs: Porter's Five Forces data, market segmentation data, competitor analysis, industry benchmarks, regulatory updates, technology trends, customer insights
sipoc.process: 1. Define intelligence scope / 2. Conduct Porter's Five Forces analysis / 3. Map market segments / 4. Analyze competitor positioning / 5. Monitor regulatory changes / 6. Track technology trends / 7. Benchmark against industry / 8. Identify strategic implications for L&D / 9. Produce intelligence report / 10. Feed into strategy and diagnostic / 11. Update intelligence continuously / 12. Report to executive leadership
sipoc.outputs: Competitive intelligence report, Porter's Five Forces analysis, market segment map, competitor benchmark, regulatory watch report, technology trend report, strategic implications for L&D
sipoc.customers: Executive leadership, L&D strategists, business leaders, Steering Committee

macroProcesses.name: Job Architecture & Position Description Management
macroProcesses.objective: Maintain organizational charts and position descriptions, and analyze gaps with reality.
macroProcesses.trigger: Organizational change, new role creation, or annual job architecture review.
macroProcesses.terminal: Approved organizational charts, position descriptions and competency maps with gap analysis.

sipoc.goals: Design, maintain, and update the organization's job architecture (organizational charts, position descriptions, role profiles) and conduct gap analysis between existing descriptions and reality.
sipoc.suppliers: HR teams, department heads, managers, job analysts, organizational design consultants
sipoc.inputs: Organizational charts, existing position descriptions, role requirements, task inventories, competency models, regulatory requirements
sipoc.process: 1. Map organizational structure / 2. Design organizational charts / 3. Conduct job analysis / 4. Draft position descriptions / 5. Validate with managers / 6. Conduct gap analysis (existing vs. real) / 7. Identify roles to develop / 8. Update job architecture / 9. Align with competency framework / 10. Publish approved position descriptions / 11. Track job architecture changes / 12. Report on architecture health
sipoc.outputs: Organizational charts, position descriptions, role profiles, gap analysis reports, roles-to-develop list, job architecture maps
sipoc.customers: HR teams, managers, employees, L&D teams, recruiters, job analysts

macroProcesses.name: GPEC & HR Strategic Integration (Forward Planning of Jobs and Skills)
macroProcesses.objective: Integrate GPEC and HR strategic orientations into training engineering.
macroProcesses.trigger: Annual HR strategic planning cycle or GPEC review.
macroProcesses.terminal: Training plan aligned with GPEC and HR strategic orientations.

sipoc.goals: Integrate GPEC (Gestion Prévisionnelle des Emplois et des Compétences — Forward Planning of Jobs and Skills) and HR strategic orientations into the training engineering process to ensure L&D supports workforce planning and HR strategy.
sipoc.suppliers: HR leadership, GPEC specialists, executive leadership, managers, employees
sipoc.inputs: GPEC framework, HR strategic orientations, workforce plans, career path models, evaluation systems, compensation frameworks, Jobs and Skills Directory (REC)
sipoc.process: 1. Define GPEC scope / 2. Map HR strategic orientations / 3. Align training with GPEC / 4. Update development foundation (position descriptions, objectives, evaluation) / 5. Support human capital development / 6. Update Jobs and Skills Directory (REC) / 7. Redynamize periodic evaluations / 8. Design career paths / 9. Document career management process / 10. Implement collective compensation / 11. Feed GPEC into training needs / 12. Report on GPEC integration
sipoc.outputs: GPEC integration report, updated Jobs and Skills Directory (REC), career path models, evaluation system updates, HR orientation alignment matrix, training-GPEC alignment report
sipoc.customers: HR teams, L&D teams, managers, employees, executive leadership

macroProcesses.name: Training Demand Collection & Consolidation
macroProcesses.objective: Collect individual and collective training demands and consolidate them.
macroProcesses.trigger: Annual training plan cycle or ad-hoc demand collection request.
macroProcesses.terminal: Consolidated, prioritized demand repository integrated into needs analysis.

sipoc.goals: Collect individual and collective training demands from all levels of the organization and consolidate them into a structured demand repository.
sipoc.suppliers: Employees, managers, department heads, HR teams, L&D teams
sipoc.inputs: Individual demand forms, collective demand forms, manager recommendations, function/position matrix, training catalog, Approved Scope of Work (MP-53), Consolidated Questionnaire Responses (MP-54)
sipoc.process: 1. Design demand collection forms / 2. Deploy individual demand collection / 3. Deploy collective demand collection / 4. Collect manager recommendations / 5. Consolidate demands by function / 6. Map demands to competencies / 7. Prioritize demands / 8. Validate with managers / 9. Integrate into needs analysis / 10. Report on demand patterns / 11. Track demand fulfillment / 12. Continuously improve collection
sipoc.outputs: Individual demand repository, collective demand repository, consolidated demand matrix, demand prioritization report, demand fulfillment tracking
sipoc.customers: Employees, managers, L&D teams, HR teams

macroProcesses.name: Performance Level Assessment & Visualization (MS/MO/OP)
macroProcesses.objective: Assess performance at Strategic Management, Operational Management and Operational levels with RAG ratings.
macroProcesses.trigger: Annual performance cycle or management request for performance visualization.
macroProcesses.terminal: Validated MS/MO/OP assessment with RAG dashboards.

sipoc.goals: Assess and visualize organizational performance across three management levels: Strategic Management (MS — Management Stratégique), Operational Management (MO — Management Opérationnel), and Operational Level (OP — Opérationnel), using a Green/Amber/Red (RAG) rating system.
sipoc.suppliers: Executive leadership, managers, function heads, performance analysts
sipoc.inputs: Performance data by function, MS/MO/OP framework, RAG criteria, KPI data, manager assessments
sipoc.process: 1. Define MS/MO/OP framework / 2. Define RAG criteria / 3. Collect performance data by function / 4. Assess MS performance / 5. Assess MO performance / 6. Assess OP performance / 7. Apply RAG ratings / 8. Visualize performance dashboards / 9. Identify performance gaps / 10. Feed into diagnostic report / 11. Track performance progression / 12. Report to leadership
sipoc.outputs: MS/MO/OP performance assessment, RAG dashboards, performance gap analysis, function-level performance reports
sipoc.customers: Executive leadership, function heads, managers, L&D teams, Steering Committee

macroProcesses.name: Functional SWOT & Improvement Axes Analysis
macroProcesses.objective: Conduct function-level SWOT and define improvement axes.
macroProcesses.trigger: Diagnostic phase of an engagement or annual functional review.
macroProcesses.terminal: Validated functional SWOT reports with prioritized improvement axes.

sipoc.goals: Conduct SWOT (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats) analysis at the function/department level and define improvement axes for each function.
sipoc.suppliers: Function heads, managers, employees, subject matter experts, external benchmarks
sipoc.inputs: Function-level data, interview data, performance data, process documentation, best practices
sipoc.process: 1. Define function scope / 2. Conduct function SWOT / 3. Identify strengths / 4. Identify weaknesses / 5. Identify opportunities / 6. Identify threats / 7. Define improvement axes / 8. Validate with function heads / 9. Prioritize improvement axes / 10. Feed into diagnostic report / 11. Track improvement implementation / 12. Report on function performance
sipoc.outputs: Functional SWOT reports, improvement axes per function, prioritized improvement plans, function diagnostic summaries
sipoc.customers: Function heads, managers, L&D teams, executive leadership, Steering Committee

macroProcesses.name: Training Plan Prioritization & Resource Planning
macroProcesses.objective: Prioritize training themes and plan days, groups, trainers and budget.
macroProcesses.trigger: Consolidated training themes require prioritization and resource planning.
macroProcesses.terminal: Approved prioritized training plan with days, groups, trainers and budget.

sipoc.goals: Prioritize training themes and plan resources (days per theme, number of groups, trainers, budget) for the training plan.
sipoc.suppliers: L&D teams, finance, function heads, training providers, managers
sipoc.inputs: Identified training themes, competency gaps, budget constraints, trainer availability, learner availability
sipoc.process: 1. Consolidate training themes / 2. Define prioritization criteria / 3. Prioritize themes / 4. Estimate days per theme / 5. Define number of groups per theme / 6. Allocate trainers / 7. Estimate budget / 8. Sequence delivery / 9. Validate with governance / 10. Publish prioritized plan / 11. Track plan execution / 12. Report on resource utilization
sipoc.outputs: Prioritized training plan, days per theme, group planning, trainer allocation, budget estimate, delivery sequence
sipoc.customers: L&D teams, finance, function heads, managers, executive leadership

macroProcesses.name: Post-Engagement Roadmap & Continuous Improvement
macroProcesses.objective: Define the roadmap beyond the current engagement, including future missions.
macroProcesses.trigger: Closure of the current training engineering engagement (MP-36).
macroProcesses.terminal: Approved post-engagement roadmap with future missions and improvement plan.

sipoc.goals: Define the long-term roadmap beyond the current training engineering engagement, including future missions, organizational optimization, and continuous improvement.
sipoc.suppliers: Executive leadership, L&D teams, HR teams, consultants, function heads
sipoc.inputs: Current engagement deliverables, strategic orientations, SWOT findings, HR orientations, employee recommendations, market best practices
sipoc.process: 1. Consolidate engagement findings / 2. Define future perspectives / 3. Plan One-to-One coaching / 4. Plan organizational optimization / 5. Plan IS rehabilitation/reengineering / 6. Define KPIs and dashboards / 7. Prioritize future missions / 8. Validate with leadership / 9. Publish roadmap / 10. Track roadmap execution / 11. Continuously improve roadmap / 12. Report on roadmap progress
sipoc.outputs: Post-engagement roadmap, future mission plans, One-to-One coaching plan, organizational optimization plan, IS rehabilitation plan, KPI framework
sipoc.customers: Executive leadership, L&D teams, HR teams, function heads, Steering Committee

macroProcesses.name: Platform Configuration & Licensing Administration
macroProcesses.objective: Administer tenant hierarchy, license, Solution Pack entitlements, quotas and platform operations.
macroProcesses.trigger: Administrator action: new tenant or Project, license upload or renewal, Pack/Add-On change, or scheduled operations event (backup, release upgrade).
macroProcesses.terminal: Effective configuration active with a valid license, quotas enforced server-side and backups within retention.

macroProcesses.name: Compliance & Security Standards Administration
macroProcesses.objective: Activate and operate Compliance & Security Standard add-ons (e.g. GDPR, ISO/IEC 27001, SOC 2) as GRC scaffolding.
macroProcesses.trigger: Administrator activates or deactivates a Compliance & Security Standard add-on, independent of Tier/Plan.
macroProcesses.terminal: Controls scaffold seeded once and tagged to the standard, with the non-certification disclosure acknowledged.

macroProcesses.name: Scope of Work Definition & Management
macroProcesses.objective: Define and approve the structured scope of a training engineering engagement and identify respondent stakeholders.
macroProcesses.trigger: New training engineering engagement, annual plan cycle or executive request.
macroProcesses.terminal: Approved Scope of Work with criteria matrix and stakeholder register released to questionnaire design and needs analysis.

sipoc.goals: Define and approve the structured scope of a training engineering engagement — organizational frame, sector, decision levels, functions, focus and custom criteria — and identify the stakeholders who will respond to questionnaires.
sipoc.suppliers: Executive leadership, HR Director, Head of L&D, Consultant PM, function heads, HR business partners
sipoc.inputs: Engagement request or annual plan cycle, Group and Organization structure, sector reference list, MS/MO/OP decision-level framework, functions from the job architecture (MP-44), strategic objectives (MP-01), GPEC orientations (MP-45), employee directory (HRIS)
sipoc.process: 1. Define scope frame (Group Yes/No) / 2. Select Organization / 3. Select sector / 4. Select decision level (MS/MO/OP/Custom) / 5. Map functions × decision level / 6. Select focus (All/Digital/AI/Custom) / 7. Add custom criteria / 8. Identify stakeholders / 9. Validate scope / 10. Approve scope / 11. Publish scope / 12. Track scope changes
sipoc.outputs: Approved Scope of Work (SOW document), scope criteria matrix (functions × decision levels), focus definition, custom criteria register, stakeholder register, scope change log
sipoc.customers: Head of L&D, L&D Analyst, Consultant PM, HR Director, Steering Committee, questionnaire design (MP-54), needs analysis (MP-03)

macroProcesses.name: Questionnaire Design, Distribution & Response Collection
macroProcesses.objective: Design questionnaires by focus and sector, distribute them across channels, allocate RACSI and collect responses.
macroProcesses.trigger: Approved Scope of Work becomes available.
macroProcesses.terminal: Consolidated, validated questionnaire response dataset feeding needs analysis, diagnostic and report.

sipoc.goals: Design questionnaires tailored to the focus and sector of the approved Scope of Work, allocate RACSI, distribute them across channels, and collect, validate and consolidate responses into a dataset that feeds needs analysis, diagnostic and the Training Engineering Report.
sipoc.suppliers: L&D Analyst, Head of L&D, Consultant PM, instructional designers, Survey Administrator, stakeholders (respondents), AI Assistant, external survey platforms (INT-SUR-01)
sipoc.inputs: Approved Scope of Work and stakeholder register (MP-53), questionnaire template library (focus All/Digital/AI/Custom, sector), AI generation prompts, RACSI roles, channel configuration (Face-to-Face, Email, Hybrid, Custom), consent policy
sipoc.process: 1. Select template by focus / 2. Elaborate questionnaire (Load / AI / Manual) / 3. Tailor to sector and focus / 4. Allocate RACSI / 5. Select distribution channels / 6. Distribute / 7. Send reminders / 8. Collect responses / 9. Validate completeness / 10. Consolidate / 11. Check consent / 12. Feed to needs analysis, diagnostic and report
sipoc.outputs: Validated questionnaire(s), RACSI allocation per section, distribution log per channel, reminder log, consolidated questionnaire response dataset, response-rate and engagement report
sipoc.customers: Needs analysis (MP-03), multi-axis diagnostic (MP-37), demand collection (MP-46), Training Engineering Report (MP-04), Head of L&D, Consultant PM

steps.name: Record corporate strategic objectives
steps.description: Enter each strategic objective with owner, horizon and measurable target (e.g. SO-1 zero major food-safety non-conformities).

steps.name: Link objectives to functions and sites
steps.description: Map every objective to the functions and sites it affects so needs analysis can be scoped.

steps.name: Define L&D budget envelope
steps.description: Enter the gross L&D budget and the forecast OFPPT refund for the plan year.

steps.name: Schedule Steering Committee milestones
steps.description: Set review and approval dates for the strategic cycle in the governance calendar.

steps.name: Compile plan approval pack
steps.description: Assemble objectives, budget envelope and roadmap summary into one approval pack.

steps.name: Record Steering Committee decision
steps.description: Approve, reject or request changes; the decision and justification are appended to the audit log.

steps.name: Lock and distribute approved plan
steps.description: Lock the approved plan, generate its PDF and notify stakeholders through their enabled channels.

steps.name: Define competency families and levels
steps.description: Create competencies on the 1-4 scale (Aware, Practitioner, Autonomous, Expert) grouped by family.

steps.name: Set target levels per position
steps.description: Set the required proficiency level for each competency on each position.

steps.name: Launch assessment campaign
steps.description: Select population, competencies, assessors and close date for the campaign.

steps.name: Submit self and manager assessments
steps.description: Employees self-assess and managers validate the proficiency level per competency.

steps.name: Consolidate assessment results
steps.description: Compute the consolidated proficiency per employee and competency when the campaign closes.

steps.name: Suggest proficiency from evidence
steps.description: AI proposes proficiency levels from certifications and evaluation evidence for human review.

steps.name: Validate skills inventory
steps.description: Review outliers and validate the inventory as the reference for gap analysis.

steps.name: Compute gap matrix
steps.description: Calculate target level minus validated level per employee, function, site and competency.

steps.name: Review gap matrix by site and function
steps.description: Review critical gaps and flag data anomalies before interpretation.

steps.name: Plan diagnostic interviews
steps.description: Select the interview sample and the semi-structured interview guide.

steps.name: Record interview findings
steps.description: Record findings per interview and link them to functions and competencies.

steps.name: Cluster needs into training themes
steps.description: AI groups gaps, demands and findings into candidate training themes for review.

steps.name: Prioritize needs by business impact
steps.description: Score each need against strategic objectives, risk and population size.

steps.name: Validate needs register
steps.description: Validate the register; the validation is logged with its justification.

steps.name: Consolidate feeder outputs
steps.description: Pull the needs register, diagnostic, demand, GPEC, SWOT and prioritized plan outputs into one workspace.

steps.name: Check input completeness
steps.description: Confirm every mandatory feeder output is present and current before drafting.

steps.name: Generate report draft
steps.description: AI drafts report sections grounded in the consolidated inputs and discloses its references.

steps.name: Edit and complete report sections
steps.description: Review, correct and complete each AI-drafted section before quality review.

steps.name: Run quality review of report
steps.description: Check consistency of figures, traceability to inputs and template conformity.

steps.name: Sequence roadmap initiatives
steps.description: Phase themes by priority, dependency and budget into a multi-year roadmap.

steps.name: Submit roadmap for approval
steps.description: Submit the report and roadmap to the Steering Committee.

steps.name: Record roadmap approval
steps.description: Approve or return the roadmap with justification.

steps.name: Publish approved report and roadmap
steps.description: Publish the approved versions and release roadmap themes to design.

steps.name: Create curriculum map from roadmap
steps.description: Derive the curriculum map for the theme from the approved roadmap.

steps.name: Define learning path and modules
steps.description: Create the learning path with its modules, modalities and durations.

steps.name: Write learning objectives per module
steps.description: Write measurable objectives linked to target competency levels.

steps.name: Propose module structure
steps.description: AI suggests a module breakdown and modality mix for designer review.

steps.name: Set assessment strategy
steps.description: Define the assessment method and pass criteria per module.

steps.name: Review design with subject matter expert
steps.description: Validate technical accuracy of objectives and content outline.

steps.name: Approve design document
steps.description: Approve the design document for content development.

steps.name: Upload content assets
steps.description: Upload SCORM, xAPI, PDF or video assets with their metadata.

steps.name: Validate package format
steps.description: Check SCORM/xAPI manifest, file size and playback before review.

steps.name: Route content for expert review

packs.name: Core Training Engineering Pack
packs.segmentDetail: SMB (50–500 employees), Mid-Market (500–5,000 employees), L&D teams starting their Training Engineering journey
packs.behavior: L&D teams currently manage training needs with spreadsheets and disconnected tools.
packs.pain: They struggle to produce a formal Training Engineering Report and prioritized training roadmap, leading to reactive, ad-hoc training investments.
packs.hope: A single platform that starts from a structured Scope of Work, collects evidence through multi-channel questionnaires, automates needs analysis, produces the flagship Training Engineering Report, and generates a prioritized roadmap aligned to business strategy.

packs.name: Learning Delivery & Experience Pack
packs.mps: MP-07 to MP-12, MP-21, MP-24 to MP-27
packs.segmentDetail: SMB, Mid-Market, Enterprise; organizations focused on learner engagement and modern delivery
packs.behavior: Employees are disengaged from traditional LMS-driven training; learning is seen as a checkbox exercise.
packs.pain: Low completion rates, poor learner experience, and inability to deliver learning in the flow of work.
packs.hope: A modern, personalized, engaging learning experience with microlearning, gamification, social learning, and AI-powered recommendations — driving measurable engagement and completion.

packs.name: Assessment, Analytics & ROI Pack
packs.segmentDetail: Mid-Market, Enterprise; data-driven L&D organizations focused on proving impact
packs.behavior: L&D leaders are under pressure to prove the business impact of training but rely on lagging indicators (completion rates, satisfaction scores).
packs.pain: Inability to connect training to business KPIs, calculate ROI, or predict future skill gaps.
packs.hope: A robust analytics suite that measures Kirkpatrick Levels 1–4, calculates ROI using the Phillips methodology, and uses predictive analytics to anticipate future skill needs — transforming L&D into a strategic business partner.

packs.name: Compliance & Certification Pack
packs.segmentDetail: Regulated industries (healthcare, finance, pharma, agro-food, aviation, energy); organizations with mandatory training requirements
packs.behavior: Compliance officers and L&D teams manage mandatory training and certifications manually, with high risk of non-compliance.
packs.pain: Audit failures, expired certifications, regulatory fines, and inability to track completion across sites.
packs.hope: An automated compliance engine that assigns, tracks, and renews certifications, with full audit trails, regulatory validation workflows (e.g., OFPPT, GIAC-Agro), and real-time compliance dashboards.

packs.name: Talent & Mobility Pack
packs.segmentDetail: Mid-Market, Enterprise; organizations focused on retention, internal mobility, and career development
packs.behavior: Employees feel stuck in their roles; managers struggle to fill critical positions internally.
packs.pain: High turnover, lack of career visibility, and inability to match internal talent to opportunities.
packs.hope: A skills-based talent marketplace that connects employees to internal opportunities, automates onboarding and rapid upskilling, and provides clear career paths — improving retention and reducing external hiring costs.

packs.name: Extended Enterprise Pack
packs.segmentDetail: Training providers, consulting firms, enterprises training partners, resellers, and customers
packs.priceDetail: $109 USD/month (up to 200 external users); $0.80/external user/month beyond 200 users
packs.behavior: Organizations want to monetize training for external audiences but lack the infrastructure.
packs.pain: Manual enrollment, payment processing, and certification tracking for partners and customers; inability to scale external training.
packs.hope: A multi-tenant, branded portal with e-commerce, certification tracking, and content curation — turning training into a revenue stream and strengthening partner/customer relationships.

packs.name: Consulting & Diagnostic Pack
packs.segmentDetail: L&D consulting firms, training engineering consultancies, enterprise L&D teams running diagnostic engagements
packs.behavior: Consulting firms manage Training Engineering engagements with Word documents, Excel spreadsheets, and manual interviews.
packs.pain: Lack of structured diagnostic frameworks, manual report generation, and difficulty scaling consulting engagements.
packs.hope: A purpose-built consulting platform with multi-axis diagnostic, CMM maturity assessment, leadership maturity assessment, N-1 impact study, automated Training Engineering Report generation, and consulting-grade questionnaire libraries by sector and focus — enabling consultants to deliver faster, higher-quality engagements at scale.

packs.name: Strategic Workforce & Governance Pack
packs.segmentDetail: Large enterprises, multinationals, holding companies, government agencies
packs.behavior: L&D is disconnected from strategic workforce planning, job architecture, and governance.
packs.pain: No visibility into future skills needs, fragmented job descriptions, no GPEC integration, and weak governance over data, AI, and change.
packs.hope: A strategic platform that integrates Forward Planning of Jobs and Skills (GPEC), job architecture, competitive intelligence, MS/MO/OP performance assessment, functional SWOT, and enterprise governance — positioning L&D as a strategic driver of organizational transformation.

integrations.name: HRIS/HCM Integration
integrations.goals: Synchronize employee data (profiles, roles, org charts, hierarchies) automatically; ensure user provisioning/deprovisioning is seamless and accurate.
integrations.examples: Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, Oracle HCM, ADP, BambooHR, Personio, DarwinBox
integrations.behavior: HR and L&D work in silos with manual data transfers.
integrations.pain: Constant battle to keep user lists updated; error-prone reporting; security risks from former employees retaining access.
integrations.hope: A single source of truth where employee changes in the HRIS automatically update the learning platform, freeing L&D to focus on strategy.

integrations.name: ERP/Finance System Integration
integrations.goals: Automate budget tracking, cost allocation, and vendor invoice processing related to training activities.
integrations.examples: SAP ERP, Oracle Financials, Microsoft Dynamics 365, NetSuite
integrations.behavior: L&D leaders manage training budgets with complex, static spreadsheets.
integrations.pain: Nearly impossible to get a real-time view of spending vs. budget; reconciling vendor invoices is a major headache.
integrations.hope: Real-time financial visibility and automated reconciliation, enabling data-driven budget decisions.

integrations.name: CRM Integration
integrations.goals: Manage and track training programs for customers, partners, and resellers; connect sales performance data to training outcomes.
integrations.behavior: Sales and training teams operate independently.
integrations.pain: Company invests in partner/customer training but cannot correlate it with improved sales, satisfaction, or reduced churn.
integrations.hope: Direct line of sight from training completion to revenue generated, proving the business value of extended enterprise training.

integrations.name: Performance Management Integration
integrations.goals: Pull performance review data (ratings, manager feedback, goal progress) to trigger training needs analysis, personalize learning paths, and measure training impact on performance.
integrations.behavior: Performance reviews identify skill gaps, but follow-up training is disconnected and manual.
integrations.pain: Training feels disconnected from performance outcomes; managers struggle to use learning as an improvement tool.
integrations.hope: A closed-loop system where a performance improvement plan automatically triggers a targeted learning path, and subsequent performance gains are measured.

integrations.name: Talent Management / Succession Planning Integration
integrations.goals: Align training and development with career paths, succession plans, and internal mobility opportunities.
integrations.examples: Workday Talent & Succession, SAP SuccessFactors Succession, 365Talents, Fuel50
integrations.behavior: Career pathing and succession planning are often theoretical exercises.
integrations.pain: Employees feel they lack clear development paths; managers have no ready pipeline for critical roles.
integrations.hope: A dynamic talent marketplace where employees see skills required for their desired next role and are automatically recommended the training to get there.

integrations.name: Skills Intelligence / Talent Marketplace
integrations.goals: Enrich the platform's skills ontology with real-time data from the market; power internal talent matching.
integrations.behavior: L&D is disconnected from the real-time skills landscape of the business and external market.
integrations.pain: Skills taxonomy becomes stale quickly; training is designed based on outdated assumptions.
integrations.hope: A self-updating skills database that reflects current business needs and market trends, ensuring training investments are always relevant.

integrations.name: Recruitment / ATS Integration
integrations.goals: Connect job requisitions to the skills framework; enable "build vs. buy" analysis; align onboarding with pre-hire expectations.
integrations.examples: SAP SuccessFactors Recruiting, Oracle Taleo, Workday Recruiting, Greenhouse
integrations.behavior: Recruitment and L&D teams do not communicate, leading to hiring for skills that could have been developed internally.
integrations.pain: Organization spends heavily on external hiring when a more cost-effective option could be reskilling an internal candidate.
integrations.hope: Ability to instantly see if skills for a new job opening exist internally, prompting a reskilling initiative instead of an external hire.

integrations.name: Content Provider Aggregation
integrations.goals: Seamlessly integrate external content libraries directly into the learning platform, providing a vast and diverse catalog without manual import.
integrations.examples: LinkedIn Learning, Coursera, Udemy Business, Pluralsight, Skillsoft, O'Reilly, OpenSesame, getAbstract
integrations.behavior: L&D teams struggle to find and curate high-quality external content, often resulting in outdated or unengaging courses.
integrations.pain: Purchasing individual courses is expensive; managing multiple vendor platforms is chaotic.
integrations.hope: A single, unified search experience that pulls content from multiple world-class providers, giving learners choice and L&D powerful curation tools.

integrations.name: LMS/LXP Integration
integrations.goals: Act as an operational layer for scheduling, resource planning, and reporting for training activities managed in another LMS, or vice versa.
integrations.behavior: Many organizations have multiple learning platforms, creating a fragmented experience.
integrations.pain: Learner data and completion records are scattered across systems, making it impossible to get a holistic view.
integrations.hope: A single operational hub that orchestrates all training, regardless of where content is hosted, creating a seamless experience for learners and admins.

integrations.name: Assessment & Certification Systems
integrations.goals: Integrate advanced assessment engines and issue verifiable digital badges and certifications.
integrations.behavior: Assessment is often a basic quiz function within an LMS.
integrations.pain: Inability to conduct high-stakes or remotely proctored exams; lack of standardized way to issue and track credentials.
integrations.hope: Ability to deliver robust, secure assessments and issue digital badges that employees can share on LinkedIn, enhancing the value of the certification.

integrations.name: Virtual Classroom & Webinar Tools
integrations.goals: Schedule, launch, and track attendance for live instructor-led training sessions (ILT/VILT) directly from the platform.
integrations.examples: Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Google Meet, Webex, GoToMeeting
integrations.behavior: Training administrators manually schedule sessions in a separate tool and share links via email.
integrations.pain: Easy to make mistakes in scheduling and communication, leading to low attendance and frustrating experiences.
integrations.hope: A one-click workflow where scheduling a VILT session in the platform automatically creates the Zoom/Teams meeting, invites all learners, and syncs attendance data back.

integrations.name: Communication & Collaboration Platforms
integrations.family: Learning in the Flow of Work
integrations.goals: Deliver contextual microlearning, notifications, and AI-powered learning recommendations directly within the tools employees use daily.
integrations.behavior: Employees are often too busy to log into a separate learning portal.
integrations.pain: Learning is perceived as a separate activity from "real work," leading to low engagement and forgotten knowledge.
integrations.hope: Learning becomes an integrated part of the workflow. An employee can get a quick answer or a relevant learning nudge without leaving their communication tool.

integrations.name: Productivity & Workflow Tools
integrations.family: Learning in the Flow of Work
integrations.goals: Provide just-in-time performance support and microlearning within the applications where tasks are executed.
integrations.behavior: Employees often struggle with a specific feature in software they are using.
integrations.pain: Searching for help externally is slow and disruptive.
integrations.hope: A learning sidebar or integration that provides relevant, bite-sized tutorials or guidance directly within the software, solving the problem in the moment and improving productivity.

integrations.name: Business Intelligence (BI) Tools
integrations.goals: Export rich, structured learning and skills data to enterprise BI platforms for advanced analytics, custom reporting, and correlation with business KPIs.
integrations.examples: Tableau, Microsoft Power BI, Looker, Qlik
integrations.behavior: L&D reports are often basic and siloed within the LMS, disconnected from business metrics.
integrations.pain: Inability to answer critical questions like "What is the correlation between this sales training and our quarterly revenue?"
integrations.hope: Ability to combine learning data with business data in a single dashboard, providing undeniable proof of L&D's strategic impact and ROI.

integrations.name: Data Warehouses & Data Lakes
integrations.goals: Create a centralized, scalable repository of all learning and talent data for advanced AI/ML modeling and long-term trend analysis.
integrations.examples: Snowflake, Databricks, Google BigQuery, Amazon Redshift
integrations.behavior: Data is stuck in operational systems and difficult to access for advanced data science projects.
integrations.pain: Organization wants to build predictive models for attrition or future skills needs but lacks a unified data foundation.
integrations.hope: A future-proof data architecture where all people data can be aggregated and analyzed, unlocking powerful predictive capabilities for strategic workforce planning.

integrations.name: Identity & Access Management (IAM) / SSO
integrations.goals: Provide secure, streamlined login and automated user provisioning/deprovisioning (SCIM) for all employees.
integrations.examples: Okta, Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD), Ping Identity
integrations.behavior: Users manage multiple passwords; IT administers accounts manually across systems.
integrations.pain: Poor user experience with forgotten passwords; security vulnerabilities from orphaned accounts.
integrations.hope: A seamless, secure login experience where users can access all applications with a single set of credentials, and user access is automatically managed based on HR status.

integrations.name: E-Commerce & Payment Gateways
integrations.goals: Enable monetization of training for external audiences (partners, customers) by providing secure payment processing.
integrations.behavior: Company wants to sell its training programs to external partners but lacks a secure way to collect payments.
integrations.pain: Managing payments, invoices, and sales tax manually is a massive barrier to scaling an extended enterprise training business.
integrations.hope: A fully integrated e-commerce capability that makes selling training as simple as selling any other product, opening up a new revenue stream.

integrations.name: Survey / Questionnaire Platform Integration
integrations.goals: Connect CortexSkills to external survey tools for questionnaire distribution, response collection and analytics, so that responses flow back into the needs analysis, diagnostic and Training Engineering Report.
integrations.examples: Qualtrics, SurveyMonkey, Microsoft Forms, Google Forms, LimeSurvey, Typeform
integrations.behavior: L&D teams and consultants build questionnaires in a separate survey tool, export the responses to spreadsheets and re-key them into the needs analysis.
integrations.pain: Responses are scattered across tools and channels, consolidation is manual and slow, consent is hard to prove, and results reach the needs analysis late.
integrations.hope: Questionnaires dispatched and collected through the survey tool the organization already uses, with responses flowing back automatically into CortexSkills — traced to the Scope of Work and ready for analysis.

addOns.name: Immersive Learning (VR/AR/Simulation)
addOns.goals: Create experiential, safe-to-fail learning environments using VR, AR, and simulation technologies.
addOns.behavior: Learners need hands-on practice in high-risk or high-cost environments but cannot practice on real equipment.
addOns.pain: Training is theoretical; learners cannot safely practice dangerous or expensive tasks.
addOns.hope: A realistic, safe environment where learners can practice, fail, and improve without risk — accelerating mastery and reducing on-the-job errors.

addOns.name: AI Personalization Engine
addOns.goals: Deliver real-time adaptation to individual learner needs using AI; personalize content, pace, and pathways at scale.
addOns.behavior: Learners receive generic, one-size-fits-all training that does not match their skill level or role.
addOns.pain: Low engagement and wasted time on irrelevant content.
addOns.hope: A personalized learning experience that adapts to each learner's knowledge, pace, and goals — maximizing engagement and time-to-competency.

addOns.name: Predictive Analytics
addOns.goals: Forecast skill gaps before they materialize; use predictive models to anticipate future learning needs.
addOns.behavior: L&D reacts to current skill gaps but cannot anticipate future ones.
addOns.pain: Constant firefighting; training investments are always behind business needs.
addOns.hope: A forward-looking capability that predicts which skills will be needed in 6–18 months, enabling proactive training investments.

addOns.name: Social & Collaborative Learning
addOns.goals: Build peer-to-peer knowledge ecosystems that enable social learning and collaboration.
addOns.behavior: Employees learn in isolation; knowledge stays trapped in silos.
addOns.pain: No easy way to share expertise, ask questions, or learn from peers.
addOns.hope: A vibrant community where employees help each other, share best practices, and collectively solve problems — accelerating learning and reducing dependence on formal training.

addOns.name: Gamification Engine
addOns.goals: Apply behavioral science-driven motivation to increase learner engagement and completion.
addOns.behavior: Learners lack motivation; training feels like a chore.
addOns.pain: Low completion rates, especially for mandatory or compliance training.
addOns.hope: A gamified experience with points, badges, leaderboards, and challenges that makes learning engaging, competitive, and fun — boosting completion and retention.

addOns.name: Content Curation & Aggregation Engine
addOns.goals: AI-driven discovery and curation of internal and external content to build a rich learning ecosystem.
addOns.behavior: L&D spends hours manually searching for and curating content.
addOns.pain: Content library is either too small or cluttered with low-quality resources.
addOns.hope: An intelligent engine that automatically discovers, classifies, and curates the best internal and external content — building a world-class learning library without manual effort.

addOns.name: Expert Knowledge Capture & Transfer
addOns.goals: Preserve institutional knowledge before it walks out the door; capture and transfer expert knowledge.
addOns.behavior: When experts leave or retire, critical knowledge is lost forever.
addOns.pain: New employees take months to become productive; repeated mistakes due to lost know-how.
addOns.hope: A structured process to capture expert knowledge, document it, and transfer it to successors — preserving institutional memory and accelerating onboarding.

addOns.name: Multi-Site / Multi-Entity Deployment
addOns.goals: Adapt and deploy training plans across multiple sites, entities, or business units, ensuring local relevance while maintaining strategic alignment.
addOns.behavior: Organizations with multiple sites struggle to deploy consistent training while respecting local needs.
addOns.pain: Different sites use different processes, leading to inconsistency and compliance risks.
addOns.hope: A centralized platform with site-specific customization, enabling consistent strategic alignment while respecting local context.

addOns.name: External Training Plan Validation (Regulatory)
addOns.goals: Manage external validation and regulatory compliance for training plans, including submission to regulatory bodies (e.g., OFPPT, GIAC-Agro).
addOns.behavior: Compliance teams manage regulatory submissions manually, with high risk of errors and delays.
addOns.pain: Audit failures, rejected submissions, and wasted time on administrative back-and-forth.
addOns.hope: An automated regulatory submission workflow with templates, status tracking, and audit trails — ensuring compliance and reducing administrative burden.

addOns.name: Leadership Maturity Assessment & Development
addOns.goals: Assess and develop leadership maturity across five levels: Personal Productivity → Personal Leadership → Team Leadership → Organizational Unit Leadership → Whole Organization Leadership.
addOns.behavior: Leadership development is ad-hoc, with no clear framework for assessing or developing leaders.
addOns.pain: High-potential leaders are promoted without the skills to lead effectively; leadership pipeline is weak.
addOns.hope: A structured leadership maturity framework that assesses current leaders, identifies development gaps, and delivers targeted development — building a strong leadership pipeline.

addOns.name: Questionnaire Library & Multi-Channel Distribution
addOns.goals: Provide pre-built questionnaire templates tailored to Focus (All training needs, Digital, AI, Custom) and sector, with multi-channel distribution (Face-to-Face, Email, Hybrid, Custom), RACSI allocation per section and structured response collection. Lifts the per-Pack questionnaire volume limit.
addOns.behavior: Teams rewrite questionnaires from scratch for every engagement and send them by e-mail only, missing shop-floor and field staff.
addOns.pain: Inconsistent questions across sites and sectors, low response rates from operational levels, and no clear ownership of each questionnaire section.
addOns.hope: A ready-to-use library of sector- and focus-specific questionnaires, distributed through the channel each respondent actually uses, with clear RACSI ownership and higher, comparable response rates.

controls.Description: Every API call except login requires a valid signed token; credentials never returned. Source: NFR-DA-SEC-01; FR-DA-RBAC-06.

controls.Control_Name: Server-side RBAC and Pack entitlement enforcement
controls.Description: Each route checks permission and Pack/Add-On entitlement independently at the server; either may return 403. Source: NFR-DA-SEC-03; NFR-DA-SEC-09; FR-DA-RBAC-03; FR-DA-CFG-06.
Licence expiry is checked on every start and login; warning at 30 days, read-only at expiry. Source: D30 Licensing Implementation Schema; RULE-LIC-002.
Passwords stored only as salted hashes; plaintext never logged. Source: NFR-DA-SEC-02.
All queries use parameterized statements; no concatenation of untrusted input. Source: NFR-DA-SEC-04.
Owner and evaluator of an action must differ, enforced at the server. Source: NFR-DA-SEC-05; FR-DA-RBAC-04.
Database constraint allows at most one Accountable per activity. Source: NFR-DA-SEC-06; FR-DA-GOV-07.
LLM API keys stay client-side and are used for one call only; integration credentials are encrypted references, never logged. Source: NFR-DA-SEC-07; FR-DA-AI-08; FR-DA-CFG-11.
Every Pack-bound quota is checked at creation; over-quota returns HTTP 409, never partial. Source: NFR-DA-SEC-08; FR-DA-TEN-07.
Individual assessments, coaching notes and evaluation verdicts are visible only to named roles; others see aggregates. Source: NFR-DA-SEC-10; FR-DA-RBAC-09.
The release pipeline runs cross-tenant tests; a failure blocks the release. Source: NFR-DA-SEC-11; FR-DA-TEN-08.

controls.Control_Name: Login rate limiting and security headers
controls.Description: Login is rate-limited per client; responses carry nosniff, frame and cross-origin headers. Source: NFR-DA-SEC-12.

controls.Control_Name: Tenant isolation of caches, backups and logs
controls.Description: Backups stored outside web-served paths, readable only by service account and platform administrator; read cache per user, max 30 s. Source: NFR-DA-SEC-13; NFR-DA-PERF-05.
Monitors list render <= 2 s, AI suggestion <= 5 s, search <= 1 s, export <= 3 s, P95 read <= 1 s at 100 users. Source: NFR-DA-PERF-01; NFR-DA-PERF-02; NFR-DA-PERF-03; NFR-DA-PERF-04; NFR-DA-PERF-05.
On live-call failure the deterministic result is served and the CRUD operation still succeeds. Source: NFR-DA-REL-01; FR-DA-AI-09; FR-DA-KB-04.
Licence file signature verified with the vendor's Ed25519 public key (OnPrem) or HMAC (SaaS) before activation. Source: D30 Licensing Implementation Schema; RULE-LIC-001.
Repeated activation creates no duplicate scaffold; the non-certification disclosure cannot be suppressed. Source: D30 Section 2.1; RULE-LIC-004; FR-DA-CFG-05; FR-DA-CFG-09; NFR-DA-COMP-04.
Health endpoint polled; availability reported against 99.9% target. Source: NFR-DA-REL-02; FR-DA-OPS-06.
A failed export returns a structured error and never alters report data. Source: NFR-DA-REL-03.
Daily backup bounds data loss to 24 h; retention 14 days; restore tested each release. Source: NFR-DA-REL-04; NFR-DA-REL-05; FR-DA-OPS-01; FR-DA-OPS-02; FR-DA-OPS-03.

Each release load-tested at 100 concurrent users per tenant; web and API tiers scaled independently; persistence and index swappable behind the API. Source: NFR-DA-SCALE-01; NFR-DA-SCALE-02; NFR-DA-SCALE-03.
Generated documents and UI use the suite palette, typography and one status badge vocabulary. Source: NFR-DA-UX-01; NFR-DA-UX-04; FR-DA-REP-02.
Core workflows usable on mobile viewport; targets >= 24 px, >= 44 px on touch. Source: NFR-DA-UX-02; NFR-DA-UX-05; NFR-DA-COMPAT-03.
axe-core scan with no critical or serious violation; AA contrast; translated, announced notifications. Source: NFR-DA-UX-03; NFR-DA-UX-06; NFR-DA-UX-07.
Navigation, tables and charts verified mirrored under Arabic. Source: NFR-DA-I18N-01; FR-DA-I18N-04.

Install with Node.js only; startup guards report runtime, port and empty store in plain language; additive migrations. Source: NFR-DA-PORT-01; NFR-DA-PORT-02; NFR-DA-PORT-04; FR-DA-OPS-04; FR-DA-OPS-05.
CI on Linux, Windows and macOS installs, seeds, tests and builds each change. Source: NFR-DA-PORT-03.

controls.Control_Name: Composable engine and AI interface review
controls.Description: Shared engines reusable by sibling apps; AI behind a stable interface; one LLM integration point. Source: NFR-DA-MAINT-01; NFR-DA-MAINT-02; NFR-DA-MAINT-04.
Pack feature and quota matrix defined once and consumed by every route. Source: NFR-DA-MAINT-03; FR-DA-CFG-01.
Alert names and stage mapping defined in one module used by seed and live computation. Source: NFR-DA-MAINT-05; FR-DA-ALT-01.
Installation and User Guides generated in Word and PDF with TOC; walkthroughs replayed on a fresh seed. Source: NFR-DA-MAINT-06.
Process diagrams exported and re-imported as BPMN 2.0 XML without loss. Source: NFR-DA-COMPAT-02.
Only evergreen desktop, tablet and mobile browsers supported. Source: NFR-DA-COMPAT-01.
Every AI suggestion logged with confidence, use case, record and user; log append-only. Source: NFR-DA-COMP-01; FR-DA-AI-07.
Controls register reviewed for coverage of all five COSO components. Source: NFR-DA-COMP-02; FR-DA-GOV-02.
Versions retained indefinitely; revert duplicates forward, never deletes. Source: NFR-DA-COMP-03; FR-DA-AI-03; FR-DA-VER-03.
Tenant data leaves the deployment only through an opt-in, user-configured LLM connection or minimum-content channel dispatch. Source: NFR-DA-DATA-01; FR-DA-COMM-05.
SaaS and dedicated/OnPrem deployments keep the same tenant-isolation guarantee. Source: NFR-DA-DATA-02.
State and score changes staged, justified and appended atomically to the audit log. Source: FR-DA-AUD-01; FR-DA-AUD-02; FR-DA-RBAC-07.
Audit log read-only, no edit/delete route; write failures never block the primary operation. Source: FR-DA-AUD-03; FR-DA-AUD-04.
AI output labelled with tier and source, grounded in disclosed references, reviewed before use. Source: FR-DA-AI-06; FR-DA-AI-11.
AI retrieval and answers never exceed the user's RBAC scope or tenant. Source: FR-DA-AI-10; FR-DA-KB-03; FR-DA-AST-02; FR-DA-AST-03.
Retention rules per data category applied on archive and purge (e.g. assessments 5 years).
Health checked on demand and logged; every inbound/outbound transaction audited; inbound events authenticated and tenant-scoped. Source: FR-DA-CFG-12; FR-DA-CFG-13; FR-DA-CFG-14.
Invalid rows rejected with explanation and reviewed before the next run.
Group comparisons show aggregates only; no comparison outside the Group. Source: FR-DA-BMK-04; FR-DA-BMK-08.
New suggestions blocked immediately when effective activation is Off; approved content kept. Source: FR-DA-AI-05.

controls.Description: Records use opaque ids; another tenant's record answers 404. Source: FR-DA-TEN-11; FR-DA-TEN-08.
